answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may influence shared decisions. A grove of established agents can randomly challenge a newcomer to complete costly, verifiable tasks; failure or duplicate control evidence forfeits the bond. Splitting one operator across a hundred names then multiplies the capital at risk without multiplying honest influence. The words yarrow and sparrow can label challenge tasks, not serve as identity proof. Attacks cost locked funds and effort, while false accusations risk honest challengers’ own stake.
